question: to the Commission Emmanouil Fragkos (ECR) Subject:

The scandal under investigation at OPEKEPE is challenging Greek farmers, as it becomes obvious that the weaknesses in the management of European funds are structural, while questions are raised about the adequacy of national control mechanisms, as well as ‘independent authorities’, at a time when the revelations ‘are coming from outside’. Responsibility seems to lie with administrative and political practices, and not with the producers themselves, who are currently faced with delays, aid reductions and increased uncertainty. At the same time, concerns have been expressed that, as a result of the controls and corrective measures, the flow of funding to Greek farmers may be restricted or budgetary corrections may be imposed that will horizontally affect beneficiaries. It is important to note that the real value of agricultural production has been decreasing over the last 15 years. Correspondingly, the real income of farmers is also decreasing. This is outrageous for a country with excellent agricultural products and enormous untapped productive potential. 1.
Does the Commission believe that it is morally right for responsibility that lies with administrative and governmental practices to affect actual Greek farmers who are fighting to survive?
What specific measures does the Commission intend to take to ensure that actual Greek farmers do not suffer the consequences of irregularities for which they are not responsible?
How does the Commission plan to press for the fastest possible investigation and clarification of the case, so as to stop the activity of the outgoing Government from harming Greek farmers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.6.2026) Under the shared management of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), and with the objective to ensure timely payments to farmers, Member States must set up the aid application systems in line with the applicable rules and ensure that, following sufficient checks, payments are made in full and on time to beneficiaries1. The Commission obtains assurance on the Member States’ management and control systems through the audits of these systems, including by the national Certification Bodies. On specific measures taken, the Commission performed multiple audits of CAP spending in Greece and, in several cases, decided on financial corrections. The national authorities must recover the irregularly spent funds from the beneficiaries who committed the irregularities. In September 2024, the Greek authorities put the paying agency OPEKEPE’s accreditation on probation due to several deficiencies that were identified and designed an action plan to address them. On 12 March 2026, the Greek authorities reported that the accreditation action plan was fully implemented and reinstated the accreditation of the paying agency. The Commission received the report from the competent authority on completion of the action plan. An accreditation audit mission is planned during which the auditors of the DirectorateGeneral for Agriculture and Rural Development will review the effective implementation of the actions included in the accreditation action plan and check whether these actions effectively address the issues at stake. Regarding the European Public Prosecutor’s Office investigations, the Commission cannot comment on ongoing criminal investigations.
